title: Convulsive status epilepticus in a child
stem: Paediatric resus. A 3-year-old girl (about 14 kg) has been fitting for 10 minutes. Her mother says she has had a cold, no previous seizures, and no medicine has been given. She is having generalised tonic–clonic movements now. HR 160, SpO2 90% in air, temperature 38.6 °C.

phases.title: Immediate care
phases.goal: Start the clock, monitoring, airway and oxygen, glucose, and access.

phases.title: Benzodiazepine
phases.goal: From the drug cart, dosed for her weight. Watch the clock: a second dose if she is still fitting.

phases.title: Second line
phases.goal: Two doses and still fitting: the next drug.

phases.title: The cause
phases.goal: Why is she fitting? Bloods, history, and cover for infection.

events.say: She is still having generalised tonic–clonic movements.
Ten minutes after the lorazepam: still fitting.
Ten minutes after the second dose: still fitting.

review.text: Buccal midazolam dose. Your notes cap it at 5 mg. APLS uses 0.3 mg/kg up to 10 mg.
Second-line drug. Your notes give phenytoin only. Since EcLiPSE and ConSEPT, APLS lists levetiracetam 40 mg/kg (max 3 g) over 5 minutes as first choice or equal to phenytoin.

notes:
Checked against the APLS algorithm for convulsive status epilepticus (APLS 7th edition, 2023 update following EcLiPSE/ConSEPT: levetiracetam as a second-line option alongside phenytoin), NICE NG217 (Epilepsies, 2022) and RCUK paediatric guidance.

At 5 minutes: first benzodiazepine — IV/IO lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg (max 4 mg), or buccal midazolam 0.3 mg/kg (max 10 mg) if no access. At 15 minutes (10 minutes later): a second benzodiazepine dose. At 25 minutes: levetiracetam 40 mg/kg (max 3 g) IV over 5 minutes, or phenytoin 20 mg/kg over 20 minutes (or phenobarbital 20 mg/kg if already on phenytoin). At 45 minutes: RSI with a senior anaesthetist. Maximum two benzodiazepine doses including pre-hospital doses.

Always check glucose early (treat under 3 mmol/L with 2 mL/kg 10% glucose) and look for the cause (fever, meningitis/encephalitis, electrolytes, trauma, toxins).

Your notes: buccal midazolam max 5 mg (APLS uses 0.3 mg/kg up to 10 mg) and phenytoin as the only second-line drug; APLS now lists levetiracetam first or equally. Lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg max 4 mg and PR diazepam 0.5 mg/kg match.

steps.label: Monitoring
steps.hint: Ask the nurse to put the patient on the monitor.

opts.t: Put her on the monitor: ECG leads and SpO2.
opts.mark: Asks for continuous ECG, NIBP and SpO2 monitoring

opts.t: Note the time the seizure started; start a clock

A–B.t: Airway: jaw thrust, suction, oral airway if tolerated; high-flow oxygen
Hold her limbs down to stop the jerking
A–B.r: Restraint does not stop a seizure and can injure her. Protect from injury.

A–B.t: Put something in her mouth so she doesn't bite her tongue
A–B.r: It can break teeth and obstruct the airway.

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: First benzodiazepine, dosed for 14 kg; a second if she is still fitting 10 minutes later.

opts.mark: First benzodiazepine at the right dose

opts.r: The adult dose: 0.1 mg/kg (1.4 mg) for 14 kg.

opts.t: Lorazepam second dose 0.1 mg/kg (1.4 mg) IV

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: Still fitting after two benzodiazepines: a second-line drug.

opts.t: Levetiracetam 40 mg/kg (560 mg) IV over 5 minutes

opts.r: More than two benzodiazepine doses causes respiratory depression without more benefit.

opts.t: Bloods: culture, FBC, CRP, U&E, calcium, magnesium, gas
Ask about head injury and access to medicines at home

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: Febrile, and meningitis or encephalitis is possible.

wrong: A third dose of lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg, then observe for 10 min

qs.a: Hypoglycaemia causes seizures and is reversible
wrong: A high glucose predicts epilepsy later in childhood
It is required before giving lorazepam

qs.a: A seizure of 5 minutes or more, or repeated without recovery
wrong: Any seizure lasting more than 1 minute
A seizure lasting more than 60 minutes
Two or more seizures within a year

badge.name: Still Waters
badge.flavor: Clock, glucose, two benzos, then levetiracetam.

cards.q: IV lorazepam dose in paediatric status?
cards.why: Repeat once after 10 minutes if still fitting.

cards.q: Levetiracetam loading dose in paediatric status?

cards.why: Cardiac monitoring: risk of arrhythmia and hypotension.
If no IV access and buccal midazolam unavailable.

cards.q: Status epilepticus continuing after second-line drug: next?
options: Oral sodium valproate via NG tube

cards.q: What not to do during a seizure?
options: Put an object in the mouth
cards.why: Risk of dental injury and obstruction.
